title: AlphaQuanter: An End-to-End Tool-Augmented Agentic Reinforcement Learning Framework for Stock Trading

task.value: Daily single-stock trading decisions (BUY/SELL/HOLD) by an LLM agent that learns via RL to orchestrate tools and acquire information on demand.
task.quote: we introduce AlphaQuanter, a single-agent framework that uses reinforcement learning (RL) to learn a dynamic policy over a transparent, tool-augmented decision workflow, which empowers a single agent to autonomously orchestrate tools and proactively acquire information on demand

architecture.value: Single ReAct-like agent: initial plan, then iterative loop of tool-based information acquisition, reasoning, and acting; trajectories scored by outcome reward plus format and tool process scores; policy trained with GRPO in verl.
architecture.quote: The workflow begins with an initial Plan generation, followed by an iterative loop with three stages: (i) identify an information gap and Acquire new evidence via a tool call; (ii) Reason over the acquired evidence to update beliefs, and (iii) Act

data.value: Five US large-cap stocks (GOOGL, MSFT, META, NVDA, TSLA); daily OHLCV and technical indicators, fundamentals, news/Reddit sentiment, and macro indicators from Yahoo Finance, Alpha Vantage and a Reddit dump.
data.quote: We focus on five stocks: Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL); Microsoft Corporation (MSFT); Meta Platforms, Inc. (META); NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA); and Tesla, Inc. (TSLA).

window.value: Train 2022-09-01 to 2024-03-30 (395 days); valid 2024-05-15 to 2024-11-14 (128 days); test 2025-01-01 to 2025-06-30 (122 trading days), with ~30-trading-day gaps.

models.value: AlphaQuanter trained on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct used to summarize Reddit posts.
models.quote: We train the AlphaQuanter agents using Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct Yang et al. (2024) as backbones, with the verl framework Sheng et al. (2025), optimizing the policy with the GRPO algorithm Shao et al. (2024).

baselines.value: Buy-and-hold; MACD and ZMR rules; FinRL A2C and PPO; Chronos-2; FinMem and TradingAgents (GPT-4o); TradingAgents with various backbones (Qwen, DeepSeek-V3.1, Kimi-K2, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o); single-agent AlphaQuanter without RL.
baselines.quote: We compare with seven categories of baselines: (1) Market: a passive buy and hold strategy; (2) Rule: classic technical trading rules, including MACD and ZMR Zhang et al. (2024a); (3) RL: traditional deep RL baselines, including A2C and PPO

headline_result.value: Over the six-month 2025 test period, AlphaQuanter-7B averaged ARR 34.94%, SR 0.65, MDD 24.93% across five stocks (3B: 23.03%, 0.43, 25.16%).

costs.value: Transaction fee rate λ = 0.001 on buys/sells; capital utilization κ = 0.9 as slippage buffer. Inference: AlphaQuanter-7B uses 4.1K tokens per decision, 0.15× multi-agent cost.
costs.quote: | \lambda | Transaction fee rate for BUY/SELL orders.

uncertainty.value: Mean over three independent runs with distinct random seeds; no confidence intervals reported. Also a rolling-window (3-month, 7-day step) robustness analysis; inter-rater α=0.78 for human eval.
uncertainty.quote: For each configuration, we report the mean performance over three independent runs (distinct random seeds) to mitigate variance.

leakage_controls.value: Chronological non-overlapping splits with ~30-trading-day gaps; tool calls with dates beyond the current decision date are heavily penalized in the reward.
leakage_controls.quote: We split data chronologically into non-overlapping train/valid/test sets, as shown in Table 4. We also insert an approximately 30-trading-day gap between successive sets to prevent leakage and look-ahead bias.

limitations.value: Bounded by predefined toolset; single-asset rather than portfolio decisions; long accumulated context from tool calls under computational constraints, needing better memory.
limitations.quote: First, the agent’s capabilities are bounded by its pre-defined toolset. It can orchestrate existing functions but cannot generate novel analytical methods. Second, our framework focuses on single-asset decision making

release.value: Code and data released on GitHub.
release.quote: Our code and data can be found at https://github.com/horizon-llm/AlphaQuanter.
